brief: Weekly US industrials/materials setup note. Geopolitical headlines over the weekend are seen pushing uncertainty higher, which keeps commodity prices elevated and is the direct driver of materials (+~300bps) outperforming industrials (-~90bps) and the broader market (-200bps) last week. AI/data-center weakness persisted, but defensives (defense, waste) rose in absolute terms rather than just outperforming, a new dynamic. Leverage and SMID names underperformed, and this uncertainty also shows up in a VIX spike and quality as the dominant factor. Prime data: US equities were net sold, driven by single-stock long-and-short selling. Info Tech was the worst performer and most net sold, led by Semis (57% of Info Tech's dollar selling). Defensive sectors (Health Care, Comm Svcs, Staples) were net bought. A third of industrials/materials names report this week. Desk setups: GE is cautious but flags 2028 guidance as upside. MMM positioning skews net negative on organic growth risk. NOC is viewed negatively on free-cash-flow and contract-loss fears. CSX short interest is rising amid an UNP/NSC merger-premium debate. PKG's containerboard crowding ranks PKG, then SW, then IP. URI is the most crowded long in machinery by elimination.
